rationale.usefulness: Documented integration with established coding surfaces, explicit fixed-model selection and usage accounting enable a practical provider-comparison pilot. The report gives concrete teaching-app, website and production-utility tasks and separates image support by surface. Installation, key handling and actual completion quality remain untested.
rationale.impact: Reducing provider-switching friction can meaningfully widen model choice for existing agent users. Evidence here establishes a beta integration and advertised economics, not a new model capability or measured ecosystem-wide gain; the impact is moderate and operational.
rationale.novelty: The integration across several terminal and desktop agents is a useful package, but hosted model routing and compatibility layers are established ideas. The report supplies no controlled evidence of a uniquely better router, and the session-versus-request discrepancy prevents treating routing behavior as a demonstrated innovation.
rationale.maturity: Detailed setup, pinning, billing and troubleshooting documentation support a real pilot. The beta warning, contradictory primary descriptions of routing frequency and surface-specific configuration make dependable production behavior insufficiently established, especially without an installation or task trial.
rationale.openness: Provider choice and named open-model endpoints improve optionality, but this path uses a hosted gateway and paid accounts. Neither the connector’s complete licensing nor every model’s deployment rights is established; hosted open-model access does not provide local inspectability or reproducibility of the routing service.

concerns: No blocking discrepancy found because the report prominently preserves the unresolved once-per-session versus per-request routing conflict.
The savings percentage and same-token counterfactual must not become an accepted-task savings claim. The report correctly separates Together, Anthropic and image charges.
